metadata.title: SDLC Identity and Attribution

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for unambiguous attribution of SDLC actions to accountable human and non-human identities without granting authority to deploy or execute.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Identity systems, CI/CD automation identities, source repositories, and audit logging within software delivery pipelines.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Solution pattern governing identity binding and attribution across SDLC activities.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines identity claims, commit signatures, pipeline actor identifiers, and audit trails as trust-relevant SDLC data.

props.name: nist-controls
props.remarks: SDLC Identity and Attribution implements identification and audit-related controls.

metadata.remarks: SDLC Identity and Attribution ensures that every SDLC action is attributable to a responsible identity. Attribution does not imply authorization, assurance, or permission to deploy or execute.

components.title: Human Developer Identity Attribution
components.description: Binds SDLC actions to authenticated human identities for accountability and auditability.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.remarks: Use of compromised or misused developer credentials.

techniques.name: Strong Authentication
techniques.remarks: Strong authentication for developers performing SDLC actions.

components.title: Non-Human (Automation) Identity Attribution
components.description: Distinct attribution of automated SDLC actors such as CI/CD pipelines, build agents, and bots.

techniques.name: Subvert Trust Controls
techniques.remarks: Abuse of CI/CD service identities to perform unauthorized actions.

techniques.name: Credential Hardening
techniques.remarks: Restricting scope and permissions of automation identities.

components.title: Attribution Logging and Traceability
components.description: Maintains immutable audit trails linking SDLC actions to identities and artifacts.

techniques.name: Event Logging
techniques.remarks: Comprehensive logging for accountability and incident investigation.

components.title: Identity Non-Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Defines what identity and attribution do not grant or imply.
components.remarks: Attribution to a valid identity does not imply authorization, approval, or permission to deploy or execute software.
